clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: During a central-line dressing change, an RN has established a sterile field. Sterile solution spills onto the field and moisture wicks through the sterile drape from the unsterile bedside table beneath it. Which action is most appropriate before continuing?

options.A: Blot the wet area with sterile gauze and continue the dressing change because the top surface of the drape remains sterile.
options.B: Cover the wet section with a new sterile drape and continue using the original field if the sterile supplies themselves appear dry.
options.C: Stop the procedure, discard the contaminated setup as needed, perform hand hygiene, and establish a new sterile field before continuing.
options.D: Move the wet sterile drape to a dry section of the table and continue as long as the central-line site has not yet been touched.

semantic_correction.rationale: The 2026 NCSBN NCLEX-RN Test Plan explicitly includes use of appropriate technique to set up a sterile field and maintain asepsis, as well as evaluation of whether aseptic technique is performed correctly, under Safety and Infection Prevention and Control. NCBI/Open RN guidance on sterile fields identifies moisture wicked from an unsterile area as contamination and emphasizes that central-line dressing changes require a critical aseptic field that must be maintained throughout the procedure. Once moisture has wicked through the sterile drape from the unsterile table, the field can no longer be relied on as sterile. C is therefore the uniquely best response: stop progression, remove contaminated materials as needed, perform hand hygiene, and re-establish a sterile field before continuing. A attempts to dry rather than correct contamination. B places another drape over a contaminated field without re-establishing asepsis. D relocates the contaminated setup but does not restore sterility. Therefore C is correct.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: When moisture wicks through a sterile barrier from an unsterile surface, treat the affected sterile field as contaminated and re-establish asepsis before continuing an invasive procedure rather than drying, covering, or relocating the contaminated setup.

scope_exclusions.entire_room_or_all_equipment_contaminate: Not asserted. The response requires discarding/replacing the contaminated setup and any affected supplies as needed, not automatically discarding unrelated sterile materials that remain uncompromised.
scope_exclusions.drying_restores_sterility: Not endorsed. Once moisture has wicked from an unsterile surface, drying or covering the area does not restore sterility.
scope_exclusions.procedure_specific_dressing_product: Not tested; the item evaluates sterile-field management rather than a particular central-line dressing product.

near_duplicate_check.note: V2-Q0775 tests Airborne Precautions for suspected measles. V2-Q0622 tests malfunctioning-equipment removal/reporting. V2-Q0271 tests hand hygiene after contact with patient surroundings/equipment. V2-Q0776 tests contamination of a critical sterile field by moisture wicking from an unsterile surface. Targeted repository search for sterile-field contamination returned no matching item before staging.

option_audit.A: Plausible attempt to preserve the setup but drying does not reverse contamination from moisture wicking through the barrier.
option_audit.B: Plausible barrier-repair response but covering a contaminated field does not re-establish the original field as sterile.
option_audit.C: Correct. It stops progression and re-establishes asepsis before continuing the invasive procedure.
option_audit.D: Plausible relocation response but moving a contaminated field to a dry surface does not restore sterility.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible best answer. The stem explicitly states that moisture wicked through the sterile drape from an unsterile table. C alone treats the setup as contaminated and re-establishes a sterile field; A/B/D attempt to preserve or relocate a field whose sterility has already been compromised.

cueing_check.note: Exact character counts were calculated from the stored strings. Correct option C is only five characters longer than B and all four choices are parallel procedural responses.
